title: Model Degradation Hinders Deep Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Deep GNNs show drastic performance degradation when stacked with many layers, limiting expressive power and exploitation of deep neighborhoods.

gap.claim: Recent studies mainly attribute deep-GNN degradation to over-smoothing, while this paper distinguishes it from model degradation.

contributions.claim: The paper disentangles graph convolution into independent Propagation and Transformation operations and separates depth into propagation depth Dp and transformation depth Dt.
The authors report that large Dt, rather than over-smoothing mainly caused by large Dp, is the major cause of deep-GNN performance degradation.

The paper presents Adaptive Initial Residual (AIR), a plug-and-play module compatible with all kinds of GNN architectures and intended to alleviate model degradation and over-smoothing simultaneously.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments support the report that large Dt is the major cause of deep-GNN performance degradation.
Experiments on six real-world datasets report that GNNs equipped with AIR outperform most GNNs with shallow architectures.
The authors report that AIR's time costs can be ignored.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs have achieved success in graph mining tasks.
Performance degrades drastically as GNNs become deeper, leading most GNNs to remain shallow.
Recent studies mainly attribute the degradation to over-smoothing.
The paper separates propagation and transformation operations and depths, then reports that large transformation depth is the major cause of degradation.
AIR is introduced to address both issues, with reported gains on six real-world datasets and negligible time cost.

source_observation.claim: Separating propagation depth from transformation depth identifies different mechanisms associated with deep-model degradation.

interpretation.claim: When depth combines multiple operations, decomposing those operations may make failure causes easier to isolate.

application.claim: Analyze or control distinct depth components separately when diagnosing degradation in layered graph models.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition generalizes beyond the reported GNN setting.

source_observation.claim: AIR reportedly improves performance while addressing model degradation and over-smoothing, with negligible time cost.

interpretation.claim: A lightweight architectural module may provide benefits by targeting multiple failure modes simultaneously.

application.claim: Consider plug-and-play residual mechanisms when extending GNN depth under both degradation and over-smoothing concerns.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify dataset characteristics, comparison details, metrics, or independent verification of the reported gains.

unknowns: The six datasets, baselines, metrics, and experimental settings are unspecified.
Implementation details and theoretical guarantees for the P/T decomposition and AIR are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide independent verification or full-text evidence.
